## Stages

This order follows the partner's approved sequence, 2026-11-06: Track A (O1, O3, O2), then Track B (O6, O4, O5).

It diverges from the brief's driver numbering, which runs seasonality, collection, funding, sample, staffing. It follows dependency and information order instead:

- O1 rests on sharp calendar variation from public release dates. It is the cheapest identified question, and its first fit measures model runtime for every later stage.
- O3's decomposition conditions how O2 reads the two-month revision.
- Track B's covariates are hand-built, slow-moving and collinear, and its answers do not change Track A's model.

The three research files' own priority-gap rankings (for example chatgpt §3.2) were not read in full. No comparison against them is claimed.

- [ ] Stage 1: Track A, O1, collection days and one-month revision scale
      Objective: Answer O1 as a written finding.
      Spec: Part A driver 2, stage 1; Part B data inventory; Part C (scale covariates, priors, validation, implementation notes).
      Gap closed: O1; Part C implemented (first part).
      Consumes: The scaffold package only.
      Produces: A monthly vintage panel of first and second prints; a release-calendar and collection-days series; a first model fit with its measured runtime on real data.
      Exit: A committed finding states the estimated effect of collection days on one-month revision scale, with its uncertainty and diagnostics. The panel, the calendar series and the runtime are recorded in the plan's Handoff.
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Track A, O3, sample vs. seasonal-factor decomposition
      Objective: Answer O3 as a written finding.
      Spec: Part A driver 1; Part C (seasonality, joint NSA/SA vintages; structural change).
      Gap closed: O3.
      Consumes: Stage 1's vintage panel, calendar series and fit runtime.
      Produces: Matched NSA/SA vintages in the panel; a fitted decomposition of the one- and two-month revisions.
      Exit: A committed finding reports each component's share of one- and two-month revision scale over time, with uncertainty.
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: Track A, O2, first-closing rate and two-month revision scale
      Objective: Answer O2 as a written finding.
      Spec: Part A driver 2, stage 2; Part C (scale covariates, identification).
      Gap closed: O2.
      Consumes: Stage 1's panel and calendar series; Stage 2's NSA/SA vintages and decomposition.
      Produces: A collection-rate series aligned to the panel; the completed Track A model.
      Exit: A committed finding states the estimated effect of the first-closing rate on two-month revision scale, net of the Stage 2 decomposition, with uncertainty.
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Track B, O6, sample size and attrition
      Objective: Answer O6 as a written finding.
      Spec: Part A driver 4; Part B data inventory (hand-built covariates); Part C (identification and confounding, shrinkage prior).
      Gap closed: O6.
      Consumes: Stage 1's vintage panel.
      Produces: A hand-built series of sample size and attrition.
      Exit: A committed finding reports the posterior for the sample-size and attrition effects on revision scale, and says what is not identified.
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Track B, O4, appropriations, continuing resolutions and shutdowns
      Objective: Answer O4 as a written finding.
      Spec: Part A driver 3; Part B data inventory; Part C (identification and confounding; party as a descriptive grouping only).
      Gap closed: O4.
      Consumes: Stage 1's vintage panel; Stage 4's covariate series.
      Produces: A hand-built series of real appropriations, continuing resolutions and shutdowns.
      Exit: A committed finding reports the posterior for the funding effects alongside the sample covariates, with the stated identification limits.
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Track B, O5, staffing
      Objective: Answer O5 as a written finding.
      Spec: Part A driver 5; Part B data inventory; Part C (identification and confounding).
      Gap closed: O5.
      Consumes: Stage 1's vintage panel; Stage 4's and Stage 5's covariate series.
      Produces: A hand-built staffing series; the completed Track B model.
      Exit: A committed finding reports the posterior for the staffing effect jointly with the funding and sample covariates, and states what about their collinearity cannot be separated.
      ROUTING: brainstorming

## Stage-spec stamp

Each stage spec's Rollout note carries this line:

> Roadmap: specs/ces-revisions-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

Retire this roadmap only after re-running the gap rubric over every row above against the accumulated system, with evidence for each verdict: the stage, the plan, Deviation notes and deferred items.

Any requirement still unmet, including the unstaged benchmark and wedge-back row, exits one of two ways: a new stage, or a deferral with a written reason.
